title: Local Development and Debugging Azure Functions
description: Set up your local development environment for Azure Functions and learn debugging techniques with Visual Studio Code.

data.text: Azure Functions can be developed, tested, and debugged locally before deploying to Azure. The primary tools are Azure Functions Core Tools and Visual Studio Code with the Azure Functions extension.

items: Azure Storage Emulator or Azurite for local storage
Visual Studio Code with Azure Functions extension

data.text: Creating and Running a Function Locally

data.title: Terminal — Initialize and Run a Function App
data.content:
# Initialize a new Functions project
func init MyFuncApp --worker-runtime dotnet-isolated

# Create a new HTTP-triggered function
cd MyFuncApp
func new --template "HTTP Trigger" --name HelloWorld

# Start the local Functions runtime
func start

# Test the function
curl http://localhost:7071/api/HelloWorld?name=Developer

data.text: Local settings store connection strings and configuration values for local development. This file is ignored by git and should never be deployed to Azure.

data.title: Azurite for Cross-Platform Development
data.text: Azurite is a cross-platform storage emulator that works on Windows, macOS, and Linux. It replaces the deprecated Azure Storage Emulator. Install it via npm: `npm install -g azurite`.

data.title: Local Development Workflow
data.description: Create a function locally, set a breakpoint, and debug it in VS Code.
steps: Create a new Functions project with `func init`
Set a breakpoint in the function body
Run the debugger in VS Code and trigger the function
Verify the breakpoint is hit and inspect variables
data.expectedOutcome: You can step through function code and inspect variables locally.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Use Azure Functions Core Tools for local development
VS Code provides full debugging support with breakpoints
data.takeaway: Local development lets you test and debug functions before deploying to Azure.
